# dsh-preset-rules

[English](README.md) | [简体中文](README.zh.md)

Keep DeepSeek Harness agent presets under a small, editable rule file — regenerated on every start, so a dsh update never leaves your presets stale.

`dsh-preset-rules` is a dsh bundle with one host plugin. On boot it reads the preset declarations that ship with your installation, applies your rules, and writes the result to `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`. That file is a normal dsh patch layer: dsh applies it after the profile layer, and its file watcher recomposes the tree when it changes.

## Why a generated file

An override written by hand goes stale: when dsh ships a new preset row, a frozen copy silently loses it. Generating the patch at every start keeps the snapshot current without any manual step, and the output stays a plain YAML file you can read, diff, and delete.

## Requirements

- dsh 0.2.x
- Node.js >= 20 (the bundled runtime is newer)

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <profile> add <this-package>
```

Or install it from the Harness UI with the plugin manager (Creator mode writes the same bundle patch).

Then write your rules:

```sh
node bin/preset-rules.js --init     # creates a starter file with commented examples
```

```sh
# $DSH_HOME/preset-rules.rules
presets = all; entry = id: time-context; action = hide()
```

The plugin never writes rules on its own: with no rules file it logs one line per start (so the first install is not silent) and changes nothing.

Start with `check` mode — either flip `mode: check` in the plugin config or run the CLI:

```sh
node bin/preset-rules.js --check
```

It prints what would change and writes nothing. Switch to `apply` (the default) once you are happy.

## Rules

One rule per line, three clauses separated by `;` (any order):

```
presets = all; entry = id: time-context; action = hide()
```

| clause | values |
|---|---|
| `presets` | `all`, an id, `{a, b}`, `not(x)`, and `+` / `-` between them |
| `entry` | `*`, `id: value`, `name: value`, `{a, b}`, `not(...)`, `+` / `-` |
| `action` | `hide()`; `disable()`, `enable()`, `set(path, value)` are reserved for 0.2 |

Binary `+` and `-` need spaces on both sides; identifiers may contain `-`, `.`, `@`, `/`. `#` starts a comment.

Examples:

```
presets = not(minimal); entry = id: time-context; action = hide()
presets = {standard, cordis}; entry = not(id: persona); action = hide()
```

Diagnostics carry `file:line:column`. An unknown preset or a rule that matches nothing is a warning; a syntax error, an unknown action, or a reserved action stops the run and leaves the previous file untouched.

## Modes

| mode | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `apply` (default) | validate, then write when the bytes changed |
| `check` | compute and print the result, write nothing |
| `off` | do nothing |

## CLI

```sh
node bin/preset-rules.js [--check|--apply] [--rules <file>] [--target <file>] [--source <dir>] [--json]
node bin/preset-rules.js --init [--rules <file>]
```

Defaults: `$DSH_HOME/preset-rules.rules` and `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml`. `--source` points at the `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` package directory; auto-detection covers both a desktop install and an npm install. Reading files inside a packaged `app.asar` requires Electron-as-node, which is what the desktop app already uses.

## Generated file

```yaml
# generated by dsh-preset-rules 0.1.0 — do not edit
# source: @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app 0.2.2-rc.1
# source-hash: sha256:…
# rules-hash: sha256:…
- id: preset-cordis
  name: '@deepseek-ai/dsh-agent-preset'
  config:
    id: cordis
    order: 4
    plugins: [ … ]
```

No timestamps: identical inputs produce identical bytes, so a start with nothing to do writes nothing.

The file is owned by this plugin. It refuses to overwrite a file that does not start with the marker above — move hand-written patches into the profile layer instead.

## Uninstall

Remove the plugin, then delete `$DSH_HOME/cordis.patch.yml` (or empty your rule file and start once). The generated layer is global to the machine, so every profile on it shares it.
